artifact.canonical_name: AUTOSAR AP and ROS 2 Collaboration Framework

sources.title: AUTOSAR AP and ROS 2 Collaboration Framework
sources.role: Author arXiv paper/preprint used to verify the architecture, evaluation scope, material claims, and limitations available in the primary text.

claims.text: The proposed framework implements a ROS 2-side bridge that converts between DDS and SOME/IP, including SOME/IP service discovery and type conversion, to connect ROS 2 nodes with AUTOSAR Adaptive applications.
The framework includes automatic generation of FIDL/FDEPL configuration from a small set of service/message identifiers and can derive conversion specifications for custom ROS 2 messages.

The paper evaluates the bridge using ROS 2 Humble/Fast DDS and vsomeip on two Ubuntu PCs, and an AUTOSAR Adaptive R20-11/QNX environment running in QEMU; seven PointCloud2 data sizes are used for latency evaluation.

limitations.text: AUTOSAR Adaptive/QNX is evaluated in QEMU rather than on an automotive target ECU/HPC.
The implementation/evaluation is tied to ROS 2 Humble, Fast DDS, vsomeip 3.4.9.1 and AUTOSAR Adaptive R20-11; interoperability across other implementations/releases requires separate evidence.

targets.target: Verify the architecture, evaluation setup, material claims and limitations reported for AUTOSAR AP and ROS 2 Collaboration Framework; preserve paper results as AUTHOR_CLAIM unless independently established.
targets.finding: The full primary text verifies the DDS-SOME/IP bridge architecture, automatic configuration generation, software versions, QEMU AUTOSAR environment, and seven-size PointCloud2 latency methodology.

editorial.why_now_note: Bridging AUTOSAR Adaptive/SOME-IP and ROS 2/DDS directly addresses mixed-platform SDV development and reuse rather than forcing one middleware stack everywhere.
editorial.rationale: Strong middleware-boundary evidence: it demonstrates a concrete conversion/configuration architecture and realistic development tooling, with the QEMU/vendor/version boundary retained.
